  • Handling Of Medico legal Cases:

1. Purpose

To deal with all medico legal cases as per the national laws

2. Scope

The Scope of the SOP is applicable to “A case of injury or ailment where attending physician after taking history and clinical examination of the patient thinks that some investigation by law enforcing agencies are essential so as to fix the responsibility regarding the case in accordance with the law of the land” Therefore, going by the above definition the scope of the SOP is applicable to the following situations:

•All cases of injuries and burns

•All accidents, RTA, factory others when likelihood of patient death or grievous hurt

•Suspected or evident sexual assault

•Suspected or evident criminal abortion

•Unconsciousness- causes known or not clear

•Suspected or evident poisoning

•Suspected or evident intoxication

•Brought dead with improper history, suspicion of offence

•Any other cases which have legal complications

3. Responsibility: Casualty Medical Officer on duty

4. Procedure

A.Registration of MLC:

•All cases as mentioned in the scope should be registered as MLC

•On arrival to the HOSPITAL, brought either by the relatives, police or self

•Entry be made in the MLC register, citing the registration no. of the case

•Whenever any medico-legal case comes to the hospital, the Casualty Medical Officer on duty should inform the Officer In charge of Police Station, giving the name, age, sex of the patient or brought dead and should start the treatment of the patient

•Casualty Medical Officer on duty to fill up the police intimation form and send it to the Concerned Police Station through the HOSPITAL Staff. Make the form in duplicate. Give original to the OC and carbon copy to be acknowledged by the OC and hand it back to the Hospital Staff for keeping as HOSPITAL copy.

B.Identification:

•The Casualty Medical Officer on duty must ensure that once a case has been registered as MLC, identification of the patient (victim or accused) is a must.

•The Casualty Medical Officer on duty must look out for and record two or more identification marks such as moles, scars, or tattoos, which are permanent in the exposed part of the body noting their color, size and location.

C.Preparing a Medico-Legal Report

•Casualty Medical Officer on duty must ensure to document the ML report by thoroughly filling up all the three components of the report viz., Preliminary, Observation and the Opinion section.

•CMO on duty should ensure that the Preliminary section of the ML report must contain the MLC registration no. , particulars of the person, date & time of arrival, date & time of starting the examination and date & time of completion of the examination etc., requisition from whom etc.,

•CMO on duty should ensure that the Observation part of the ML report be filled up properly which must include the Facts observed on examination, the investigation sent, and the preliminary treatment given.

•CMO on duty must give his unbiased opinion, based on facts observed and lab findings. Provisional opinion can be given pending investigation

•The CMO on duty should prepare ML report in duplicate. Original copy to be handed over to the Requisition police officer who should acknowledge the receipt of the report by signing on the duplicated copy of the report which is retained as the office copy.

•The CMO on duty should use indelible ink. Hand writing should be eligible. The report should be clear, concise and complete. Avoid abbreviations and acronyms. Avoid overwriting. Avoid superlatives. Avoid technical terms

•Never scratch the report. Avoid correction materials. Avoid erasers. Draw a line through the error. Initial above error.

•The CMO on duty should sign at the bottom of every page and in the last page must put his/her signature, name and designation

•All medico-legal papers must be stamped/ marked MLC.
